rulings.challenge_claim: The song-frame identification at the onset verse and the close at 27:5 both rest on English rendering choices that the Hebrew of the cited verses does not carry; and the quote/gloss pairing inverts the Hebrew word order.
rulings.grounds: All three arms verify, and the challenge is if anything too generous on the third. ARM 1: the onset verse carries no song lexeme at any tier. oshb:Isa.27.2 reads בַּיּ֖וֹם הַה֑וּא כֶּ֥רֶם חֶ֖מֶד עַנּוּ לָֽהּ (byte tier) - six tokens, none of them the song noun or its cognate verb, which stand together at יוּשַׁ֥ר הַשִּׁיר (oshb:Isa.26.1, byte tier, unique in the book at sweep: 1 verse) and whose consonantal skeleton stands at 9 verses book-wide (sweep: 9 verses), the nearest being oshb:Isa.26.1 itself. The row nevertheless calls this 'a second, separate song frame' and its signal keys carry a song-announcement formula, so a frame class with a real instance one chapter earlier is imported into a verse whose bytes carry no such form. The construal of עַנּוּ לָֽהּ as an order to sing is defensible on its own, and the unit_type is not what is being challenged - the defect is a FORMULA claim asserted without the form present in the cited verse. ARM 2, the sharpest and most mechanically curable: the quote/gloss pairing inverts the Hebrew. The row pairs the English clause “In that day, sing to her,” (web:Isa.27.2) with the whole six-token run and then presents “A pleasant vineyard!” (web:Isa.27.2) as a quotation INTRODUCED by that run - but כֶּ֥רֶם חֶ֖מֶד (oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier), the words so rendered, are the THIRD and FOURTH tokens inside the very run cited, standing before the verb. The 'formula, then introduced quotation' sequencing exists only because the English reorders the clause; the full English is “In that day, sing to her, “A pleasant vineyard!” (web:Isa.27.2). Quote/gloss parity is campaign law and the gloss must be re-cut. ARM 3: the close's first arm is where the English quotation mark falls - “Let him make peace with me.” (web:Isa.27.5) - and the pointed bytes of oshb:Isa.27.2 through oshb:Isa.27.5 carry letters and accents and no quotation delimitation at any tier, so that arm is a tier-4 rendering artifact and can never set an edge; the material inside the English quotation is itself first-person divine speech, which the delimiter does not track. ADDED, and it strengthens rather than softens the challenge: the second, byte-grounded arm of the close does NOT survive as stated either. The row argues a new opening at 27:6 from the English “In days to come, Jacob will take root” (web:Isa.27.6) and quotes no Hebrew there at all. The bytes give הַבָּאִים֙ (oshb:Isa.27.6, byte tier), a bare participial form unique in the book (sweep: 1 verse) and not a member of the staged tier-1 frame spine; the noun that makes it read as a dated formula is supplied by the translation. So both halves of this row's closing warrant are carried by the rendering. Correct as written: the two Hebrew runs the row does quote reach byte tier in their cited verses, the SAMEKH after oshb:Isa.27.1 is cited under the right type as single-witness, the inventory records no further mark inside Isa.27.2-Isa.27.5 as the row says, and the cross-part vineyard relation to Isa.5.1-Isa.5.7 is properly quarantined as typed metadata.
rulings.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: re-cut the gloss so quote and Hebrew agree - either splice the onset's two tokens alone and gloss כֶּ֥רֶם חֶ֖מֶד separately in its own place in the run, or quote the whole run against the whole English clause “In that day, sing to her, “A pleasant vineyard!” (web:Isa.27.2); the introduced-quotation sequencing must go. (2) Replace the song-FRAME assertion with what the bytes support: an onset formula plus a construal of עַנּוּ לָֽהּ (oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier), stated as a construal, with the song-announcement signal key dropped or re-keyed, since the formula's real instance is at oshb:Isa.26.1 and not here. (3) Re-warrant the closing edge from bytes: splice הַבָּאִים֙ יַשְׁרֵ֣שׁ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.27.6, byte tier), add oshb:Isa.27.6 to boundary_evidence_refs, and say what the form is (a bare participial onset, not a staged frame class); the English quotation mark may remain only as an explicitly tier-4, non-driving corroboration. No boundary change is proposed. TESTS: no field rests an edge on translation punctuation or on a noun the translation supplies; every English gloss maps to the Hebrew tokens actually inside the run it is paired with; every formula/frame claim names a form present in the cited verse's own bytes with its tier.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's load-bearing reason for overriding a marked internal break is a plural English pronoun that does not stand in either of the two verses it is claimed for, and a feminine-suffix chain reaching back across the row's own front seam is undisclosed; the onset is also called a fresh formula though it is a bare participial form.
rulings.grounds: Two arms hold; the suffix-chain arm is byte-false as framed. ARM 1 UPHELD, and it is the load-bearing one: strongest_rejected_alternative sets aside a single-witness setumah recorded after MT 27:6 on the ground that 'the pronoun "them" opening Isa.27.7 has no antecedent besides Jacob and Israel named in Isa.27.6'. No such pronoun stands there. oshb:Isa.27.7 opens הַכְּמַכַּ֥ת (byte tier), an interrogative-comparative construction, and its suffixes are third masculine singular - מַכֵּ֖הוּ הִכָּ֑הוּ and הֲרֻגָ֖יו (byte tier) - while the English “Has he struck them as he struck those who struck them?” (web:Isa.27.7) renders them collectively and does not put 'them' at the head of the verse either. The referential conclusion may still be reachable from those 3ms forms, but the row quotes no Hebrew from 27:7-8 at all and never makes that argument, so a tier-3 mark is overridden on a ground available only in the rendering. ADDED PRECISION: the row's rationale extends one English 'them' across 'Isa.27.7-8', but the suffixes at oshb:Isa.27.8 are third feminine singular - בְּשַׁלְחָ֣הּ תְּרִיבֶ֑נָּה (byte tier) - so a single pronoun is being carried over TWO different suffix classes. Held as a form-class reading, since no morphology layer is staged. ARM 2 REFUTED AS FRAMED: there is no 3fs chain 'straddling the 27:5 | 27:6 seam'. The feminine suffixes run oshb:Isa.27.2 (עַנּוּ לָֽהּ), oshb:Isa.27.3 (נֹֽצְרָ֔הּ לִרְגָעִ֖ים אַשְׁקֶ֑נָּה) and oshb:Isa.27.4 (אֶפְשְׂעָ֥ה בָ֖הּ אֲצִיתֶ֥נָּה), all byte tier - and then STOP: oshb:Isa.27.5 carries first-person forms instead (יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה שָׁל֖וֹם לִ֑י, byte tier), oshb:Isa.27.6 carries no pronominal suffix at all, and oshb:Isa.27.7 is 3ms. They resume only at oshb:Isa.27.8, two verses past the seam. The real observation - a feminine object reappearing at 27:8 that may reach back to the vineyard - is worth disclosing, but it does not cross this row's front edge as a chain and cannot argue continuity there. ARM 3 UPHELD: הַבָּאִים֙ (oshb:Isa.27.6, byte tier) is unique in the book (sweep: 1 verse) and is a bare participial form, not a member of the staged tier-1 frame spine; calling it 'a fresh formula' while quoting the English “In days to come, Jacob will take root” (web:Isa.27.6), which supplies the noun, labels a class the bytes do not carry. Correct as the challenge concedes: the two Hebrew runs the row quotes reach byte tier, and the SAMEKH after oshb:Isa.27.6 and after oshb:Isa.27.11 are correctly typed and correctly keyed to the Hebrew witness. The row is already held at reduced confidence with its frontier flag set, which is the right posture for this stretch.
rulings.remedy: (1) strongest_rejected_alternative: rewrite the override on Hebrew ground or drop it. It must splice מַכֵּ֖הוּ הִכָּ֑הוּ (oshb:Isa.27.7, byte tier) and name the suffix class as a byte-checkable, held form-class claim, and it must stop attributing one plural pronoun to 27:7 and 27:8 together, since בְּשַׁלְחָ֣הּ תְּרִיבֶ֑נָּה (oshb:Isa.27.8, byte tier) is a different class; add oshb:Isa.27.7 and oshb:Isa.27.8 to boundary_evidence_refs. Keep the mark tier-3 weak and non-driving either way. (2) boundary_rationale: replace 'a fresh formula' with what the bytes give - splice הַבָּאִים֙ יַשְׁרֵ֣שׁ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.27.6, byte tier) and describe it as a bare participial onset, noting that the dating noun is supplied by the rendering. (3) Do NOT add a feminine-suffix 'chain across the front seam' - if the 27:8 feminine object is disclosed at all, it must be cited as a resumption after oshb:Isa.27.5-27.7 carry none. No boundary change proposed. TESTS: every pronoun/suffix claim in the row names a verse, a form, and a tier, and is held where no morphology layer supports it; no claim describes a suffix class that a sweep of the cited verse's bytes contradicts; the reference mirror shows every verse argued in prose present in boundary_evidence_refs.

rulings.challenge_claim: The split of the two adjacent day-formula verses is defended by a generalized pattern claim with no digit and by importing a different device class, while the linking form shared by both onsets is never weighed; the long form stands in 13 verses book-wide and these two are its only adjacent pair.
rulings.grounds: The disclosure residue is real but small, and two of the challenge's own load-bearing claims are byte-false. BYTE-FALSE 1 - the exclusivity claim: the waw-prefixed long onset stands at 13 verses book-wide at skeleton tier (sweep: 13 verses - oshb:Isa.7.18, 7.21, 7.23, 10.20, 10.27, 11.10, 11.11, 17.4, 22.20, 23.15, 24.21, 27.12, 27.13), and that set contains TWO adjacent pairs, not one: oshb:Isa.11.10 | oshb:Isa.11.11 as well as oshb:Isa.27.12 | oshb:Isa.27.13. 'These two are its only adjacent pair' does not survive the sweep it cites. BYTE-FALSE 2 - the identity claim: the two onsets are NOT the identical form at byte tier. וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.27.12) and וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.27.13) each re-collate at byte tier in their own verse but differ from each other in their accents; they agree only at accent_stripped and skeleton tier. Calling them 'identical' is exactly the accent-blind framing the tier-disclosure standard exists to prevent. WHAT SURVIVES, and it is a low-grade disclosure gap rather than a warrant failure: the row carries no digit and no tier for the onset formula it makes its splitting ground, and the bare form it treats as a unit onset two rows earlier is a much larger object (sweep: 45 verses at skeleton tier) than the long form here, so two distinct spellings do sit under one undifferentiated signal key. REFINED on the massa arm: the header class IS a different object - exactly 10 verse-initial sites, bounding parent oracles, none of them in this chapter - so the analogy borrows warrant from a class the row is not using. But this is an appeal to analogy, not a blended sweep, so it is a warrant-strength defect rather than a count-discipline breach. Separately and more concretely, the same sentence appeals to what 'this campaign otherwise treats' - a governance-process appeal that row prose should not carry in any field. REFINED on the unweighed-counter-reading arm: the row DOES weigh the merge - its strongest_rejected_alternative is precisely that reading, and it notes the shared destination itself. What is genuinely missing is the grammatical arm, that the waw on both onsets is a sequencing form which reads at least as readily as one continuing announcement. Correct as written: the quoted run reaches byte tier, and the SAMEKH after oshb:Isa.27.11 and after oshb:Isa.27.12 are correctly typed, correctly keyed to the Hebrew witness, and disclosed single-witness and non-driving.
rulings.remedy: (1) strongest_rejected_alternative: delete the appeal to campaign practice and to the header class; re-warrant the split from this row's own bytes - the two onsets agree at accent_stripped tier and differ at byte tier, each opens a distinct image, and a single-witness setumah stands between them (tier-3, non-driving) - and add one clause weighing the sequencing reading of the waw rather than leaving it unanswered. (2) boundary_rationale: give the onset formula a tier and a digit with its unit named (the long form at 13 verses book-wide at skeleton tier), and distinguish it from the bare form so the signal key is not carrying two spellings. No boundary change proposed. TESTS: no field appeals to campaign practice, a governing document, or a device class the row is not itself using; every recurrence claim names a tier and carries a digit with its unit; the word 'identical' appears only where a byte-tier collation supports it.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row closes the book's 27:13|28:1 frame seam without quoting the frame form that makes it a seam, and explains the missing mark there with a generalization the mark inventory contradicts.
rulings.grounds: Both arms verify exactly. ARM 1: the closing seam is argued from the parent grouping ('the closing verse of its book-level parent grouping, so this row's own close is fixed by that larger seam') and from the row's own onset, never from the following verse's bytes. web:Isa.28.1 appears as a bare reference with no oshb: counterpart anywhere in the row, and the form that makes 28:1 a seam - the verse-initial ה֗וֹי (oshb:Isa.28.1, byte tier), a member of the 20-site verse-initial woe inventory - is never quoted. A frame-based seam claim owes the frame form and its role in the cited verse's own bytes. The asymmetry is visible across the seam pair: the Isa.28.1-Isa.28.13 row on the other side of this very join DOES quote that form byte-true. ARM 2: the row states that no mark follows Isa.27.13 and that this is 'expected since it is the book's own frame-seam verse'. The absence itself is TRUE - the parashah inventory records no petuchah or setumah at MT 27:13 - but the explanation is contradicted by the inventory. Of the eight verses that close a parent grouping in this architecture, FIVE carry a mark - petuchah at MT 12:6, MT 35:10 and MT 39:8; setumah at MT 48:22 and MT 55:13 - and only MT 1:1, MT 27:13 and MT 66:24 do not. Every digit in the challenge checks out. So a tier-3 absence is given explanatory work on a layer where absence is never evidence in either direction, and the generalization it is given is false besides. CLARIFICATION, not a defect: MT 27:13 does carry one paseq seg (single-witness, count-only). That is a different layer with no symmetry obligation, so its non-mention is not a gap - but the row's flat 'no mark in the inventory' wording should not be read as covering it. Correct as written: the row's own onset run and its trumpet run both match oshb:Isa.27.13 at byte tier, and the setumah after MT 27:12 at the front seam is correctly typed and correctly keyed to the Hebrew witness.
rulings.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: splice ה֗וֹי (oshb:Isa.28.1, byte tier) into the closing-seam sentence, name its role as a verse-initial woe onset opening the next series, and add oshb:Isa.28.1 to boundary_evidence_refs, so the seam is engaged in the bytes on both sides of the join. The parent-grouping close may stay as corroboration but cannot be the only warrant. (2) device_notes: cut the explanatory clause 'which is expected since it is the book's own frame-seam verse'. State the absence flatly as a single-witness, tier-3 observation that is not treated as evidence in either direction, or drop the sentence entirely. No boundary change proposed - the seam is fixed architecture. TESTS: the seam claim carries a pointed splice from oshb:Isa.28.1 that re-collates at byte tier; the reference mirror shows oshb:Isa.28.1 present in boundary_evidence_refs; no field assigns explanatory or structural meaning to the absence of a parashah mark.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row declines an internal cut at 28:5 without disclosing that the verse opens with the very day-formula treated as a unit onset four times in the immediately preceding chapter and that the mark layer brackets exactly the rejected pair, while the counter-argument that holds it in is made from the English with no quoted form and no tier; the remnant and plene/defective observations are likewise unquoted, and all four mark references are written under a WEB coordinate prefix.
rulings.grounds: Every arm verifies, and the severity is right. ARM 1, the core: oshb:Isa.28.5 opens בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (byte tier) - the same bare verse-initial formula that this cluster's own preceding rows treat as a unit-opening driver at MT 27:1 and MT 27:2, and in its waw-prefixed long form at MT 27:12 and MT 27:13 - and the parashah inventory records a SAMEKH after MT 28:4 and another after MT 28:6, bracketing PRECISELY the 28:5-28:6 pair the row declines to cut. The row's strongest_rejected_alternative is a single sentence naming the rival and neither of its corroborations, so the strongest reading against the row's own choice is stated at its weakest. Both marks do appear in boundary_evidence_refs, so the disclosure layer is complete; what is missing is the connection between them and the rival they support. ARM 2: the argument that holds the pair inside the span - that the crown motif keeps running - is made from “a crown of glory and a diadem of beauty to the residue of his people” (web:Isa.28.5) with no quoted form and no tier, although the byte evidence is strong and available: לַעֲטֶ֣רֶת צְבִ֔י (oshb:Isa.28.5, byte tier) is the third of exactly 3 sites of the crown noun in this chapter and 4 book-wide (sweep: 4 verses at skeleton tier - oshb:Isa.28.1, oshb:Isa.28.3, oshb:Isa.28.5, oshb:Isa.62.3). ARM 3: the remnant identification is English-only too - לִשְׁאָ֖ר עַמּֽוֹ (oshb:Isa.28.5, byte tier) is the plain remnant noun, and the row's own signal key names the remnant family, an object this book splits four ways on one root, so the form owes its bytes. ARM 4: the plene/defective observation in device_notes is byte-true and unquoted - שִׁכֹּרֵ֣י (oshb:Isa.28.1, byte tier) against שִׁכּוֹרֵ֥י (oshb:Isa.28.3, byte tier). A spelling claim is a byte-checkable claim under the same discipline as a digit. ARM 5: all four mark references are written under a WEB coordinate prefix although the parashah layer is read from the Hebrew witness and keyed to its numbering; the arithmetic lands only because this chapter is identity-numbered, and the immediately preceding rows key the same object correctly at MT 26:21, MT 27:1, MT 27:6, MT 27:11 and MT 27:12. This is model territory, not a machine catch - the staged sweeps pass on these rows - which is why it needs recording: the same habit inside either offset zone would be a Tier-0 disclosure failure. Correct as written, and independently confirmed: the crown pair the row does quote is handled right - עֲטֶ֤רֶת גֵּאוּת֙ and עֲטֶ֥רֶת גֵּא֖וּת differ at byte tier and agree once accents are stripped, exactly as the row labels it; the woe onset at the row's own front edge IS quoted byte-true, which is the half of this seam pair that the Isa.27.13 row omits. POLICY NOTE for routing, not a ruling: whether a bare day-formula onset cuts a row INSIDE a hoy-onset complex is not settled by the operative rules - the formula is not a member of the staged tier-1 frame spine, and the woe category carries no internal-cut rule of its own. That reading is boss territory; the work order below is disclosure only.
rulings.remedy: (1) strongest_rejected_alternative: rebuild the rival at full strength before rejecting it - splice בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.28.5, byte tier), name the SAMEKH after MT 28:4 and after MT 28:6 as bracketing exactly that pair (tier-3, single-witness, non-driving), and then give the reason the pair stays in. (2) boundary_rationale: replace the English-only crown and remnant arms with splices - לַעֲטֶ֣רֶת צְבִ֔י and לִשְׁאָ֖ר עַמּֽוֹ (oshb:Isa.28.5, byte tier) - carrying the crown noun's digit and unit (sweep: 4 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, 3 in this chapter) and naming which remnant object of the four is meant. (3) device_notes: quote both spellings in the plene/defective sentence, שִׁכֹּרֵ֣י against שִׁכּוֹרֵ֥י, with the tier named. (4) Re-key all four mark references to the Hebrew witness (oshb:) to match the layer they are read from and the preceding rows' practice. No boundary change proposed here; any actual cut at 28:5-28:6 is a proposal for boss adoption, never author work. TESTS: the rejected alternative names every corroboration the bytes and the inventory supply for the reading it rejects; every device, spelling, and remnant claim carries a pointed splice re-collating at byte tier plus a tier label; every parashah reference in the row is keyed to the Hebrew witness; the crown digit names its unit and its tier.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the high confidence understates the live rival at the Isa.28.16 koh-amar frame, which the row rejects with only a generic addressee-continuity claim rather than the stronger subordinating evidence available in the bytes. OL: both of the row's edge arguments are made without any Hebrew, the label it puts on its close-seam verse is contradicted by that verse's bytes, and the same object takes two witness keys in one reference list.
rulings.grounds: The two items are DISTINCT in what they touch - LF the internal rival and the confidence band, OL the two edges and the reference keys - but they share ONE root cause, which neither packet names: this row systematically splices past the causal connector that opens the verse it is quoting. LF UPHELD on substance: oshb:Isa.28.16 opens לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ (byte tier), and the row's splice begins at the messenger formula, dropping the particle. That particle is the stronger warrant the row does not use - it ties the divine reply directly to the covenant-with-death quotation of 28:15 as its answer - while the reason actually given for declining the rival cut is a generic 'same addressee and frame carry through'. REFINED on the second half: the confidence comparison with neighbouring rows is factually accurate (the Isa.28.1-Isa.28.13 row sits at medium, the Isa.27.6-Isa.27.11 row at medium_low) but band-consistency with neighbours is not itself a rule; the curable defect is the omitted particle and the generic rival wording, and the confidence band follows from repairing those. OL UPHELD, with one tier sharpened. Front seam: it is the row's strongest signal and carries no byte arm at all - the bytes give שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אַנְשֵׁ֣י לָצ֑וֹן (oshb:Isa.28.14, byte tier), the addressee standing in the last two of those tokens, and that full summons formula stands at 3 verses book-wide at SKELETON tier (sweep: 3 verses - MT 1:10, MT 28:14, MT 66:5) and at 2 verses at byte tier (MT 1:10, MT 28:14); the challenge's digit is right for the skeleton object and the tier belongs with it. Close seam: the row describes 28:23 as 'a fresh vocative onset', but oshb:Isa.28.23 reads הַאֲזִ֥ינוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ קוֹלִ֑י הַקְשִׁ֥יבוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ אִמְרָתִֽי (byte tier) - six tokens, four imperative forms and two objects, no addressee noun and no vocative particle - so the label sits on a verse whose bytes do not carry it. Unclaimed bracket: the scoffer root does frame the span end to end, לָצ֑וֹן (oshb:Isa.28.14) against אַל תִּתְלוֹצָ֔צוּ (oshb:Isa.28.22), each byte tier and each standing at exactly 1 verse book-wide - a root-level link across two attested spellings, correctly cited per spelling by the challenge and not a byte-true recurrence. Keys: web:Isa.28.13 and web:Isa.28.15 carry the parashah citations while oshb:Isa.28.15 carries the ketiv/qere citation in the same list - the SAME verse under two witness keys for two objects both read from the Hebrew witness. NEW FINDING neither packet reached: the connector-eliding habit also operates at the row's OWN front edge, where it matters most. oshb:Isa.28.14 opens לָכֵ֛ן (byte tier) and the English reads “Therefore hear Yahweh’s word, you scoffers, that rule this people in Jerusalem:” (web:Isa.28.14) - the row's quotation starts after 'Therefore'. A backward-pointing causal connector at the opening verse argues continuity with the material closing at 28:13, and the row's 'a fresh addressee opens this row' claim never engages it. The petuchah after MT 28:13 corroborates a break on tier-3 weak grounds but cannot carry that argument by itself. Correct as written: the one Hebrew run the row does quote is byte-true and its speaker class is named as divine, which is the right discipline on a formula this book uses on both a divine and a royal-messenger side; the doubled ketiv/qere at MT 28:15 is disclosed and kept out of quotation.
rulings.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale, front seam: splice לָכֵ֛ן שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אַנְשֵׁ֣י לָצ֑וֹן (oshb:Isa.28.14, byte tier) INCLUDING the causal connector, add oshb:Isa.28.14 to boundary_evidence_refs, carry the summons-formula digit with its unit and tier (sweep: 3 verses book-wide at skeleton tier), and state why the backward-pointing connector does not bind this verse to the unit closing at 28:13. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: re-cut the internal rival so it engages לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ (oshb:Isa.28.16, byte tier) with the particle included, and re-check the confidence band once the rival is stated at full strength. (3) boundary_rationale, close: drop the 'vocative' label - the bytes at oshb:Isa.28.23 give an imperative-summons onset; re-key the signal accordingly, and note the scoffer-root bracket per attested spelling, explicitly NOT as a byte-true recurrence. (4) Re-key the two parashah references to the Hebrew witness so the whole list reads on one witness. No boundary change proposed. TESTS: every Hebrew splice in the row begins at the head of the clause it is quoting, connector included, and re-collates at byte tier; no form-class or speech-class label is applied to a verse whose bytes do not carry the form; every parashah and ketiv/qere reference in the row is keyed to the Hebrew witness; the confidence band is re-derived after the rival is restated.

rulings.challenge_claim: The summons the row builds its onset and its type on is quoted only in half, the vocative label it records is not present in that verse's bytes, and the disputation evidence actually inside the span goes uncited.
rulings.grounds: All four arms verify. ARM 1: the row states that 'the Hebrew doubles the summons verb pair' and then splices only הַאֲזִ֥ינוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ קוֹלִ֑י (oshb:Isa.28.23, byte tier). The doubling lives in the unquoted second colon, הַקְשִׁ֥יבוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ אִמְרָתִֽי (oshb:Isa.28.23, byte tier); the full verse is הַאֲזִ֥ינוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ קוֹלִ֑י הַקְשִׁ֥יבוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ אִמְרָתִֽי. The run actually cited displays one pair, not the doubling claimed for it - a quote that does not carry the feature it is offered as evidence for. ARM 2: the recorded signal and the rationale both call the onset a vocative, but oshb:Isa.28.23's six tokens are four imperative forms and two objects, with no addressee noun and no vocative particle; the row's own English, “Give ear, and hear my voice! Listen, and hear my speech!” (web:Isa.28.23), carries none either. An imperative-summons onset is what the bytes give, and a form-class label is a byte-checkable claim. ARM 3: the type rests on that summons form alone, and the form is not distinctive - it stands at 5 verses book-wide at skeleton tier (sweep: 5 verses - MT 1:10, MT 8:9, MT 28:23, MT 51:4, and MT 64:3 = web:Isa.64.4, the dual correctly carried by the challenge in the offset zone) - spread across openings of very different speech classes, so it under-determines the applied category on its own. ARM 4: the evidence that would carry the typing sits inside the row's own span and is uncited - the verse-initial interrogatives הֲכֹ֣ל (oshb:Isa.28.24, byte tier) and הֲלוֹא֙ (oshb:Isa.28.25, byte tier) open the case the row says the unit is making. MITIGATING, and worth recording against the severity: this row DOES carry the operative-category deviation disclosure its label requires, argued on formal rather than subject-matter ground, and it holds itself at reduced confidence with its frontier flag set - the honest posture. The defect is that the formal ground it names is quoted in half and the in-span evidence that would settle it is left out, not that the label was taken carelessly. Correct as written: the close against the following woe onset is byte-defensible, and the SAMEKH after MT 28:29 is correctly typed as single-witness - though it too is keyed to the WEB witness rather than to the Hebrew one the layer is read from, the same keying defect this writer part carries across its rows.
rulings.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: extend the splice to the whole verse, הַאֲזִ֥ינוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ קוֹלִ֑י הַקְשִׁ֥יבוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ אִמְרָתִֽי (oshb:Isa.28.23, byte tier), so the run displays the doubling the row claims for it. (2) Replace the vocative label with an imperative-summons onset in the prose AND in the recorded signal key, since no addressee noun or vocative particle stands in the verse. (3) Add the in-span typing evidence: splice הֲכֹ֣ל (oshb:Isa.28.24) and הֲלוֹא֙ (oshb:Isa.28.25), both byte tier, as the verse-initial interrogatives that carry the disputation reading, and add both refs; carry the summons form's digit with its unit and tier (sweep: 5 verses book-wide at skeleton tier), disclosing that the form alone does not fix the category. Keep the existing deviation disclosure. (4) Re-key the parashah reference to the Hebrew witness. No boundary change and no unit_type change proposed. TESTS: every quoted run displays the feature it is cited for; no form-class or speech-class label survives that the cited verse's bytes do not carry; the typing sentence cites at least one in-span form with a tier; the parashah reference is keyed to the Hebrew witness.
